steps.answer:
July is Barcelona’s peak summer month. The weather is typically hot and humid, with daytime highs around 29 °C and lows near 20 °C, very little rain and long daylight (about 15 hours). While the climate is pleasant for beach‑going and outdoor cafés, the city is also at its most crowded; tourist sites, beaches and streets are busy, and prices for accommodation tend to be higher.

If you enjoy lively atmospheres, festivals and don’t mind the heat and crowds, July can be a great time. If you prefer milder weather and fewer tourists, you might aim for late spring (May‑June) or early autumn (September‑October), which the guide notes offer warm, pleasant conditions with less congestion.
